title: Dimension at a point of a quotient of a polynomial ring over a field: n minus the difference of heights
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $S=P/I$ with quotient map $\pi:P\to S$, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime ideal of $P$ containing $I$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of a commutative ring $A$ let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $t\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t$ of prime ideals of $A$ with $\mathfrak p_t\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Let $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ (computed in $S$) and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$ (computed in $P$) are integers with $0\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$, and $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q).$$

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270: for a surjection S' -> S of finite type k-algebras, dim_{x'} Spec S' - dim_x Spec S = height(p') - height(p)) applied to S' = P = k[x_1,...,x_n], with dim_{x'} Spec P = n (Lemma Tag 00P1, label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, line 28222, and Lemma Tag 00OP, label lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660); exactly the identity c = height(q') - height(q), 'in other words dim_q(S) = n - c (see Lemma 00P2)' in the statement of Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909)

proof.text: (Setting.) $P$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (the identity $P\to P$ is a surjection from a polynomial ring in $n$ variables [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]), and so is $S=P/I$ (via $\pi$). $P$ is an integral domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] (take $D=k$, $I=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there). Hence $(0)$ is a prime ideal of $P$, contained in every prime ideal of $P$, so $(0)$ is the unique minimal prime ideal of $P$, and $P/(0)=P$. Also $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is a prime ideal of $P$ (the preimage of a prime ideal under a ring map) containing $I=\pi^{-1}(0)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270), proof 'Immediate from Lemma 00P1' (the hypotheses: S' = P -> S a surjection of finite type k-algebras)

proof.text: (Lemma 00P1 at both points; heights are finite.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ at $\mathfrak q$ and to the finite type $k$-algebra $P$ at $\mathfrak q'$ (step 1): all quantities below are finite and $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim S_{\mathfrak q}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q),\qquad \dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=\dim P_{\mathfrak q'}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q').$$ By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ (the supremum of lengths of chains of primes of $S$ ending inside $\mathfrak q$, as in the statement), and that of $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$. So $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$ are integers, both $\ge0$ (the chain consisting of the single prime $\mathfrak q$, resp. $\mathfrak q'$, has length $0$), and $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q),\qquad\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q'),$$ with all terms integers $\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270), proof 'Immediate from Lemma 00P1'; Lemma Tag 00P1 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, line 28222); height = dim of the localization, Definition Tag 00KF (label definition-height)

proof.text: (The residue fields agree: $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] (with $R=P$, the ideal $I$, $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q'$) the map $\lambda:P_{\mathfrak q'}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\pi(r)/\pi(s)$, is a well defined surjective ring map; it is $k$-linear because $\pi$ is a $k$-algebra map. Let $\mu:P_{\mathfrak q'}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ be $\lambda$ followed by the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; it is surjective onto a field, so $\ker\mu$ is a proper ideal of the local ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}$, hence $\ker\mu\subseteq\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'}$ (the maximal ideal). Conversely, for $r\in\mathfrak q'$ we have $\pi(r)\in\mathfrak q$, so $\lambda(r/s)=\pi(r)/\pi(s)\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$; hence $\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'}\subseteq\ker\mu$. So $\ker\mu=\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'}$ and $\mu$ induces a bijective $k$-algebra map $\kappa(\mathfrak q')=P_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, an isomorphism of field extensions of $k$. A $k$-algebra isomorphism carries subsets algebraically independent over $k$ bijectively onto such subsets (a polynomial over $k$ vanishes on a family iff it vanishes on its image), so by the definition of transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree] $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270), proof 'Immediate from Lemma 00P1' (the identification of the residue fields of p and p' left implicit in 'immediate')

proof.text: (Lemma 00P2.) Subtracting the two identities of step 2 and using step 3 (all terms are integers): $$\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)-\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q).$$

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270), proof 'Immediate from Lemma 00P1'

proof.text: ($\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=n$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components] applied to the finite type $k$-algebra $P$ at $\mathfrak q'$, $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)$ is the maximum of $\dim(P/\mathfrak r)$ over the minimal primes $\mathfrak r$ of $P$ contained in $\mathfrak q'$; by step 1 the only one is $\mathfrak r=(0)$, so $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=\dim P$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. $P\ne0$, so it has a maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] (applied to the ideal $0\ne P$). Since $P$ is a finite type $k$-algebra and a domain, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] gives $\dim P=\dim P_{\mathfrak M}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] gives $\dim P_{\mathfrak M}=n$. Hence $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (label lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660: dim k[x_1..x_n]_m = n) with Lemma Tag 00OS (label lemma-dimension-spell-it-out, line 27763) and Lemma Tag 00OT (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, line 27787); the value dim_{x'} Spec P = n is what the statement of Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909) uses when it writes 'dim_q(S) = n - c (see Lemma 00P2)'

proof.text: (Conclusion and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$.) By steps 4 and 5, $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$. By steps 2 and 5, $n=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')\ge0$, so $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270), proof 'Immediate from Lemma 00P1'; Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909)

proof.text: ($\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$.) Let $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_t$ be a chain of prime ideals of $S$ with $\mathfrak q_t\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Then $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_0)\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_t)\subseteq\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$ are prime ideals of $P$ (preimages of primes under a ring map), and the inclusions are strict because $\pi$ is surjective, so $\pi(\pi^{-1}(J))=J$ for every ideal $J$ of $S$ and $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_{i-1})=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$ would give $\mathfrak q_{i-1}=\mathfrak q_i$. So every length $t$ occurring in the supremum defining $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ occurs in that defining $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$, and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$. With step 2 and step 6: $0\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$.

lean.statement: theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_polynomial_quotient_eq_height_difference {k : Type u} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) [q.IsPrime] : ∃ h h' : ℕ, q.height = (h : ℕ∞) ∧ (q.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).height = (h' : ℕ∞) ∧ h ≤ h' ∧ h' ≤ n ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt (⟨q, inferInstance⟩ : Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I))) = ((n - h' + h : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
